hints.content:
The x-coordinates of the points where the graphs of the equations $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ intersect are the solutions of the equation $f(x)=g(x)$.

In our case, $f(x)=\sqrt{6x+7}$ and $g(x)=6$. We already have $f$ graphed, and the graph of $g$ is a horizontal line. Let's add it and see what we get.

[[☃ image 1]]

Both $f$ and $g$ are now graphed, and the solution of $f(x)=g(x)$ can be found by looking for their intersection points.

options.alt: A square root function graph and a horizontal line on an x y coordinate plane. The x- and y- axes scale by one. The graph starts around the point (negative one, zero) and increases from left to right through points (three, five) and (seven, seven) going towards infinity. The horizontal line is at y equals six and intersects the square root function graph at one point.

hints.content:
The graphs intersect where the $x$-coordinate is approximately $5$.

[[☃ image 1]]

hints.content: In conclusion, an approximate solution to the equation is $x\approx 5$.
